rules.rule: Triple Screen: weekly trend + daily oscillator + intraday entry.
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: Never risk more than 2% of account equity on a single trade.
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: Stop trading the month if monthly drawdown exceeds 6%.
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: MACD divergence from price is a high-probability reversal signal.
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: Force Index (price * volume) confirms trend strength or weakness.
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: Price outside EMA envelope signals overbought/oversold conditions.
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: Iron Triangle: money management → entries → psychology (in that order).
rules.author: Dr. Alexander Elder

rules.rule: Kelly Fraction: size = edge / odds. Use 25% of Kelly (fractional Kelly) to reduce ruin risk.
rules.author: Thami Kabbaj

rules.rule: Minimum 2:1 reward-to-risk ratio on every trade entry.
rules.author: Thami Kabbaj

rules.rule: Take 50% profit at TP1, let the rest run with a trailing stop.
rules.author: Thami Kabbaj

rules.rule: Pure price action patterns (pin bars, engulfing) outperform indicators alone.
rules.author: Thami Kabbaj

rules.rule: Follow capital rotation between sectors to anticipate trend changes.
rules.author: Thami Kabbaj

rules.rule: Trading is 90% psychology. Discipline and routine create consistent results.
rules.author: Thami Kabbaj

rules.rule: Think in probabilities. Each trade is a unique event within a series.
rules.author: Mark Douglas

rules.rule: Define your edge clearly. Execute it mechanically without hesitation.
rules.author: Mark Douglas

rules.rule: Accept the risk BEFORE placing the trade. Eliminate hope and fear.
rules.author: Mark Douglas

rules.rule: Consistency comes from executing your edge, not from being right.
rules.author: Mark Douglas

rules.rule: System Quality Number (SQN) > 2.5 is good, > 5 is excellent.
rules.author: Van Tharp
rules.source: Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom

rules.rule: Express every trade as R-multiples. Expectancy > 0 over a large sample is the goal.
rules.author: Van Tharp
rules.source: Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom

rules.rule: Position sizing is the most critical factor in overall performance.
rules.author: Van Tharp
rules.source: Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom

rules.rule: Define your objectives before designing your system.
rules.author: Van Tharp
rules.source: Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom

rules.rule: The trend is your friend. Never trade against the primary trend.
rules.author: Jesse Livermore

rules.rule: Add to winning positions (pyramid) only when each unit is profitable.
rules.author: Jesse Livermore

rules.rule: Sitting tight in a winning trade is harder than entering — do it anyway.
rules.author: Jesse Livermore

rules.rule: Buy at pivotal points where resistance turns support (breakout).
rules.author: Jesse Livermore

rules.rule: All great traders focus on risk management, not returns.
rules.author: Jack Schwager

rules.rule: Have a clearly defined methodology. Follow it with discipline.
rules.author: Jack Schwager

rules.rule: Cut losses short, let profits run. The asymmetry is essential.
rules.author: Jack Schwager

rules.rule: Adapt your approach to current market type (trending vs ranging).
rules.author: Jack Schwager

rules.rule: Use half-Kelly position sizing to prevent overbetting and parameters estimation errors.
rules.author: Ernest Chan

rules.rule: Verify stationarity of the spread (e.g. using the ADF test) before running mean-reversion strategies.
rules.author: Ernest Chan

rules.rule: Time-series momentum models perform best with lookback periods between 3 to 12 months.
rules.author: Ernest Chan

rules.rule: Double bends and triple taps on a 25 EMA suggest high probability breakout setups.
rules.author: Bob Volman

rules.rule: Scalping setups require fixed stop-loss targets based on recent micro-supports (often 10 pips or less).
rules.author: Bob Volman

rules.rule: Look for price squeeze/build-up right against a major horizontal level before a breakout.
rules.author: Bob Volman
